chapter: Erroll Garner, the 1952 arrest and Florida
title: Garner's drummers Harold Wang and Shadow Wilson; dates for Paris and the Three Deuces
summary: Shadow Wilson joined in 1950; the Paris trip and Three Deuces dates are discussed with Willard.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Shadow joined him in '50. This first drummer that he had when he came back from Paris didn't pan out. His name was Harold Wang. He was half Chinese and Negro. And we called him Chink. But he wanted to play with sticks, and by playing with Erroll Garner, he thought he was a star, you know, and he was going to be heard, and he was drowning Erroll out with sticks, you know. So at this time, Erroll asked me, he said, 'Man, can't you do something with him?' I said, 'No, I can't do anything with him. This is your group.' You know.
Erroll went to Paris in, what, late '49?
No, early '49, because he had been in the Three Deuces.
He played the Three Deuces in July,
With Oscar Pettiford and J. C. Heard?
I think so. I remember the Three Deuces had not had jazz, and they were restarting a -- they had not had jazz for awhile, and they were starting a jazz policy again with Erroll's opening.
That's what they were announcing, and that was like about July, June or July, but I think it was July of '49.
And I think Oscar was with him.
Well, I didn't know anything about the Three Deuces starting a jazz policy. I had worked in the Three Deuces before I had worked with Erroll Garner.

Yeah. It had had a jazz policy during the heyday of 52nd Street, but by 1949 there wasn't any music, or there was very little music on 52nd Street and the Deuces had had some other kind of policy and then they were going back.
